stem.en: Put the slow fire in order, from sugar to coin.

text.en: Hexokinase clamps glucose with one coin; glycolysis splits it into two pyruvate, filling two buckets and earning two coins net.
Pyruvate enters the mitochondrion, loses a carbon as carbon dioxide, and becomes acetyl-CoA.
The Krebs cycle strips the acetyl's electrons into carriers and lets its carbons go as breath.
The electron transport chain hands the electrons down a staircase of pullers to oxygen, pumping ions across the inner wall.
The proton gradient flows back through ATP synthase, which spins and presses about twenty-six coins.
In the leaf, light lifts electrons from water twice, fills NADPH and a dam, and the Calvin cycle spends both to make sugar from air.
